# RG Flow — Renormalization Group for Constraint Graphs

The continuous limit from the other direction.

Shows how a **constraint graph changes as you coarse-grain it** — the discrete dual of the [ZHC→Yang-Mills](https://github.com/SuperInstance) convergence. ## Concept In physics, the **Renormalization Group** describes how a system's behavior changes as you change the observation scale. For our fleet: as we coarse-grain a constraint graph (merging nearby nodes, averaging edge weights), the topological invariants (β₁, Laman rigidity, holonomy) flow toward a fixed point. This is the inverse of the ZHC→Yang-Mills convergence: it shows what our discrete constraints look like at coarser resolutions. ``` Fine-grained ZHC_ym Continuous constraints ──────────────► Yang-Mills ▲ │ │◄────── RG Flow ────────┘ (this tool) ``` ## Usage ```bash # Random geometric graph (500 nodes, 5 RG steps) python3 rg.py flow --graph random --nodes 500 --steps 5 # 2D lattice with periodic boundaries python3 rg.py flow --graph lattice --size 32 --steps 4 # Watts-Strogatz small-world python3 rg.py flow --graph small-world --nodes 200 --k 4 --p 0.3 --steps 3 # Compare different sizes python3 rg.py compare --sizes 100,250,500 --graph random # Mathematical background python3 rg.py theory ``` ## Example Output ``` ================================================================================ Renormalization Group Flow Graph: Random-Geometric (N=500, r=0.158) ================================================================================ -------------------------------------------------------------------------- Step | V | E | β₁ | V-2 | ε | Laman | deg | Phase -------------------------------------------------------------------------- 0 | 500 | 8328 | 7829 | 498 | 14.72 | 8.35 | 33.31 | 🚨 EMERGENT 1 | 25 | 72 | 48 | 23 | 1.09 | 1.53 | 5.76 | 🚨 EMERGENT 2 | 9 | 13 | 5 | 7 | -0.29 | 0.87 | 2.89 | ✅ RIGID 3 | 5 | 7 | 3 | 3 | 0.00 | 1.00 | 2.80 | ✅ STABLE 4 | 5 | 7 | 3 | 3 | 0.00 | 1.00 | 2.80 | ✅ STABLE ⚡ 5 | 5 | 7 | 3 | 3 | 0.00 | 1.00 | 2.80 | ✅ STABLE ⚡ -------------------------------------------------------------------------- ▶ Fixed point detected at step 4. The RG flow converges to a stable phase. ▶ At the fixed point the system is Laman-rigid (ε ≈ 0). Emergence has been coarse-grained away. ``` ## Key Invariants | Symbol | Name | Meaning | |--------|------|---------| | V | Nodes | # of super-nodes at current scale | | E | Edges | # of constraint edges | | β₁ | First Betti number | E − V + C — cycle space dimension | | ε | Rigidity margin | β₁/(V−2) − 1 | | Laman | Laman ratio | E/(2V−3) — >1 = redundant, <1 = underconstrained | ## Phase Classification - **EMERGENT** (ε > 0.5) — redundant constraints, rich topology - **APPROACHING** (0.05 < ε ≤ 0.5) — near the Laman boundary - **STABLE** (|ε| ≤ 0.05) — Laman-rigid, critical - **RIGID** (ε < -0.05) — underconstrained ## Requirements Zero. Pure Python 3, stdlib only. No dependencies. ## Push ```bash git init git checkout -b main git add -A git commit -m "Initial: RG flow simulator for fleet constraint graphs" git remote add origin git@github.com:SuperInstance/rg-flow.git git push -u origin main ```
